# sim_rendered — golden rendered-pbp fixtures (generated by sdv-py)

One file per **(league, provider)** pair: the full rendered play-by-play of a
single seeded simulated game, generated end-to-end by sdv-py's own sim
renderers. Unlike every other fixture directory (real captured payloads),
these are **generated artifacts** — the renderer contract made concrete —
committed so that any change to the sim engines, the provider template
registry (`sportsdataverse/_common/play_text.py`), or the renderers shows up
as a reviewable play-by-play diff.

## Provenance

- Generator: `tools/sim_fixtures/build.py` (seed 7). Regenerate everything
  with `uv run python -m tools.sim_fixtures.build`.
- Inputs are the committed REAL capture fixtures listed in each file's
  `meta.source_fixtures` (v3 pbp for nba/nbagl, ESPN summaries for
  wnba/mbb/wbb/nfl/cfb, statsapi pbp for mlb, api-web pbp for nhl) — the same
  payloads the engine conservation/distribution gates run on. Shelves, name
  pools, officials, lineups, bullpens, and RTSS context are all fitted from
  those payloads at build time.
- The matrix is every league crossed with its family's canonical providers,
  PINNED in the generator's `PROVIDERS` dict (runtime `register_provider()`
  calls never change the committed contract; shipping a new canonical
  dialect means extending the pin and regenerating):
  - basketball (`nba`, `nbagl`, `wnba`, `mbb`, `wbb`) × `nba_stats`, `espn`,
    `ncaa_stats`
  - football (`nfl`, `cfb`) × `nfl_gsis`, `espn`
  - baseball (`mlb`) × `mlb_statsapi`
  - hockey (`nhl`) × `nhl_rtss`

## Reading the files

`meta` carries league/family/provider/seed/source fixtures/final score (no
timestamps — the build is fully deterministic, verified across processes);
`rows` is the rendered log, one JSON row per line so diffs read as
play-by-play.

Note: within a league, different providers are **independent seeded games**,
not one game re-textured — provider-gated emissions (block/steal rows,
substitution pairs, timeout variants, boundary rows) consume different rng
draws, so the walks diverge after the first gated event.

## Drift gate

`tests/test_sim_rendered_fixtures.py` rebuilds every pair in-process and
asserts exact equality with the committed file. If it goes red, a renderer /
template / engine change altered the contract: eyeball the diff, then
regenerate + commit the fixtures in the same change.
